voyager1.lightTimeNote: Approximate Earth-to-Voyager 1 light time for late October 2026 (about 172 AU); NASA expects it to pass one light-day in November 2026.
voyager1.tracksNote: Illustrative 70 m DSN schedule, not the real one: one 8-hour track a day at 06:00-14:00 UTC (Goldstone or Madrid), with 22 October missed (antenna maintenance). Every track can command.

voyager2.lightTimeNote: Approximate Earth-to-Voyager 2 light time for late October 2026 (about 144 AU). Voyager 2 is far south of the ecliptic, so only the Canberra complex sees it, and only the 70 m DSS-43 can send it commands.
voyager2.tracksNote: Illustrative Canberra schedule, not the real one: one 8-hour track a day at 20:00-04:00 UTC; every third track is DSS-43 (can command), the others an array of 34 m dishes that can only listen.

common.overheadNote: Estimated BPv7 primary + payload block headers per bundle. The Merkle leaf and branch carried in each bundle are counted from the real bundle.
